title: Every count from one dated pull
statement: Keep every count, figure, rule and setting in one named, dated, re-runnable source, and derive every document and copy from it rather than editing each by hand.
example: One course's email said 52 lessons and 745 items and its infographic 47 lessons and 713, all citing one data pull.
detail: An outside review of the reading project's first course found its own materials disagreeing on lesson and item counts, though all of them cited the same data pull dated 18 June 2026 (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0081-g3-reviewer-feedback-raw-2026-07-02-reading-explorers-v2-review-verbatim.qmd`). The next course's rule was that every count in every document traces to one named pull with a date, with a render-truth manifest as the one source (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0236-g5-package-build-facts-and-g3-fixlist-apply-2026-07-02.qmd`). A consistency linter for stale numbers helped but was not enough: stragglers survived green runs, so a broad search followed it, and downstream counts were recomputed after every fix wave (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0089-parent-claude-sessions-worklog-2026-07-09.qmd`). Errors are fixed in the one source and counts recomputed after each fix, and no number is carried over from another group or slice.
against: The fix that removes the registries sat on an unpushed branch when it was recorded, so staging still carried them (`grade3-reading/knowledge_bot/knowledge/kb-0200-content-audio-review-traps.qmd`).
